body.text: The investigative journalist whose stories kicked off a police investigation into broadcaster Alan Jones is giving evidence in his criminal trial.

Mr Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 counts of indecent assault and sexual touching relating to five men, many of whom spoke to Sydney Morning Herald (SMH) journalist Kate McClymont before they made a police complaint.
The reporter published a series of stories from late 2023 that contained accounts from a number of men who alleged Mr Jones indecently assaulted them.
Some of her interviewees are not complainants in this trial. Follow live coverage.

Court breaks for lunch
McClymont will return to the courtroom after the break at 2pm.
'You're not looking for sexy phrases'
In another audio recording played to the court, Complainant C could be heard telling McClymont that Jones had asked him for nude photos.
"I didn’t engage in that stuff," the complainant could be heard saying.
McClymont told the court she asked for those text messages from Jones, but she never saw the texts.
In another interview clip, McClymont could be heard asking Complainant C if Jones would ever put his hand down his pants or grope him.
"He'd go the grope," Complainant C replied.
"He'd go the grope," Complainant C replied.
That same quote was later used in a headline in McClymont's story outlining the man's allegations.
McClymont rejected the suggestion she had referred to the alleged behaviour as groping because she wanted a "catchy" headline or quote for her story.
"You’re not looking for sexy phrases to put in a story, you're having a conversation with someone," she said.
Audio from interview with complainant played
The court heard Complainant C told McClymont about an incident where Jones had placed a hand on his leg while the two were in a car.
The court was played a section of the audio recording from that interview.
McClymont could be heard suggesting to Complainant C that he was trapped as he was the one driving the car, to which the complainant said "absolutely trapped".
Bashir put to McClymont that she put the suggestion to Complainant C because she knew it would make "a catchy quote".
McClymont said she quoted Complainant C as saying he was "absolutely trapped" in her article.
Conversation with complainant examined
McClymont is now being asked about a phone conversation she had with Complainant C in September 2023.
The court heard the complainant, who was a former colleague of Jones, revealed his identity to McClymont and detailed allegations against the broadcaster on that occasion.
They later met face to face, with the court hearing Complainant C gave McClymont consent to take notes and record their conversation.
They spoke for over an hour, the court heard.
Court resumes
Proceedings are back underway and McClymont has returned to the courtroom.
McClymont warned not to speak to media
The court has broken for morning tea.
Judge Glenn Walsh warns McClymont she "may be approached" by her journalist peers in the break and reminds her not to speak with anyone about her evidence.
He tells her there was an "unfortunate" incident involving Hadley earlier in the trial, and McClymont promises not to speak to anyone.
Witnesses are all advised not to speak to media while they are under oath.
Judge Walsh has previously expressed disdain after seeing footage of reporters approaching Hadley on his way into court during his evidence.
Court will resume at midday.
Questions about contact with Hadley and FitzSimons
McClymont told the court she did not recall speaking to Ray Hadley about Jones, saying it was instead writer Peter FitzSimons who spoke to Hadley in 2019.
She is taken to a phone log which she agreed showed FitzSimons attempted to call her on the evening of October 15, 2019.
In a subsequent email he sent to the SMH that night, FitzSimons wrote that he had "just spoken to an authoritative source", the court heard.
McClymont agreed Hadley was the source referred to in the message, and that she understood he was offering FitzSimons information about Jones.
Tensions within 2GB revisited
McClymont is now being questioned about her knowledge of a supposed plan within 2GB for then-radio host Ray Hadley to unseat Jones from his breakfast program in 2019.
Hadley, who previously gave evidence to the trial, confirmed a supposed "promise" made to him by managers at the time, that he would take over Jones's broadcasting slot.
When asked whether she was aware of the reported plans within the radio program at the time, McClymont shook her head and said "possibly", but explained that she couldn't recall exactly.
The trial previously heard Hadley spoke to a former colleague of Jones that same year, who alleged that he was indecently assaulted by the veteran broadcaster on eight separate occasions.
That man, known as Complainant C, later detailed his allegations against Jones to McClymont, who published his story in 2023.
Courtroom scenes
Jones is sitting in the same chair he has sat in for most of the previous 54 days of this trial, taking notes.
He has a small notebook and is regularly given a copy of the exhibits being discussed so that he can follow along.
He is flanked by his legal team, who he often speaks to quietly during proceedings.
McClymont was sent out of the room for about five minutes while there was some legal argument, but the issue has been resolved and she has returned.
'Not my area of expertise'
McClymont is being asked about the impact her reporting about Jones had on the SMH’s subscriber numbers and advertising revenue.
"That is not my area of expertise," she said.
Bashir also put to McClymont that Jones was a "divisive figure".
"If you say so," McClymont replied.
"He's cast as conservative leaning?" Bashir asked.
"By some people, yes," McClymont responded.
Evidence in chief finishes
McClymont has now finished her evidence in chief.
Jones’s barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC has started her cross-examination of the reporter.
The editor of the SMH Jordan Baker and deputy editor Nick Ralston are in court to support McClymont.
No payment offered to complainants, court told
McClymont says none of the complainants mentioned in her reporting were offered payment for providing information about Jones.
She was asked if she declined to provide police with notes or recordings taken by her or another reporter from when she spoke to the complainants and other witnesses.
She said some of the material was confidential and the recordings "were not available to me at that time".
Correspondence given to police

McClymont says she sought further comment from Jones and his legal team before the publication of several other stories, which outlined allegations made by a number of complainants in the current proceedings.
She did not send Jones draft copies of the articles prior to publication, the court heard.
She remembers an occasion when she received a reply directly from Jones via text.
The reporter said she provided all correspondence with Jones and his legal team to the police in a statement she made on August 30, 2024.
Key Event
Proceedings underway
We’ve got straight into it this morning, with McClymont answering questions about an article outlining allegations of abuse against Jones in December 2023.
The reporter confirms she sought comment from Jones by text and email two days before the first story was published in the Sydney Morning Herald.
McClymont says she did not receive a response from Jones, but she thought she did get a response from his lawyers.
Key Event
McClymont arrives at court
Kate McClymont arrived at court to a large media pack.
Asked how she was feeling about today's evidence, the journalist responded, "Fine."
Word appears to have got around that McClymont was due to give evidence, because the courtroom has once again attracted members of the public, as well as a larger contingent of media.
She will face questions from the Crown first, about her involvement in reporting on Jones's alleged conduct.
She will then be cross-examined by Jones's defence team, who have accused her, among others, of being part of a media conspiracy to bring down their client.
Key Event
What has the court heard so far?
This case is being heard in the local court in a judge-only trial.
The court has previously heard in relation to McClymont:
• Complainant C agreed to meet her in 2023 after she contacted him about his experiences with Mr Jones.
• The Sydney Morning Herald (SMH) published an article about Mr Jones in December 2023 detailing allegations against him.
• McClymont also spoke to or contacted 2GB employees and an ex-politician during research into the story.
• Author and journo Peter FitzSimons said he spoke to Complainant C about his experience with Mr Jones. FitzSimons said he passed his notes from the call on to McClymont.
• Complainant H reached out to McClymont after her coverage. His allegations were published in May 2024 in the SMH.
McClymont to give evidence soon
Welcome to live coverage of investigative journalist Kate McClymont's evidence in court today.
The author and award-winning reporter is giving evidence about her coverage of allegations against the defendant in the Sydney Morning Herald.
